problems: The red cloth tails fall apart: the last balls in each tail blob are too small and too far apart, so they show as loose red droplets under the tails, which look like dripping liquid.
The cloth wrap is a plain cylinder whose flat light end face shows like an open hole, so it reads as a red tube on the rope, not a cloth bound and tied around the knot.
The coil's turns spread far along its axis and, with the z turn, show as a long helix like a spring, not a tight hand coil of rope.

The coil's turns are stacked straight back in depth with the same radius, so the camera sees one thick ring, like a spring seen end-on. It shows no separate rope turns and the card doesn't read as a coiled lariat at once. Fan the turns: shift each one sideways and down a little and vary its size, so several separate strands show.

The coil is a small, narrow ring next to the loop, and the two read together as a pair of glasses rather than a lasso. Make the coil bigger and rounder so it is the main mass, with the open loop still the wider of the two.
The loop is a near-perfect circle almost in the card plane, which flattens it. Tilt it further back in depth so it reads as an open oval noose, not a flat hoop.
The red cloth's tails are two thick, parallel, rounded fingers that look like teeth or a fork, not cloth. Make them flatter, wider and pointed, and spread them apart, one longer than the other.
